We are doing our best so the people are not afflicted, but the enemy is doing its absolute best so we won’t succeed,” President Masoud Pezeshkian said during a speech on Sunday morning, alluding to the six-month US-Israel war on Iran.After US President Donald Trump threatened to target Iran with the “most crushing economic operation” ever undertaken against any country, the Iranian rial hit a new all-time low of 2 million rials per the US dollar in Tehran’s open market on Sunday afternoon.On Friday, Pezeshkian noted that the price of fuel in Iran is considerably lower than in most countries in the world.He said his administration pays 1.3 million rials (65 US cents at the current rate) per litre of petrol produced by refineries.

articles.title: Kinmen: The Sleepy Fishing Island That Could Be East Asia’s Biggest Flashpoint
articles.excerpt: “If you look over there, you can see the propaganda sign. It reads ‘unite China under one country two systems,’” a fisherman told me. I was standing surrounded by old rusted anti-tank spikes on the beach of Kinmen, an island administered by Taiwan, but geographically a part of China’s Fujian province. At this closest point, it feels like you can reach out and touch the skyscrapers of China’s Xiamen city, which is just 2 miles across the water. The fisherman comes here every day with his rod and a bucket of bait. He knows the skyline of Xiamen like the back of his hand. “I don’t worry about China,” he tells me, “Life here is very peaceful, and we keep to ourselves.” This view is held by many residents of Kinmen, who view themselves neither as Taiwanese, nor as Fujianese. They take pride in their local identity. The coastline of China’s southeastern Fujian province is littered with hundreds of small islands, many of them relatively nondescript. However, two of them stand out as remnants of a Cold War that has never truly ended: Kinmen and Matsu. In 1949, China’s Nationalist Party, the Kuomintang (KMT), led by Chiang Kai-shek was facing defeat against Mao Zedong’s communists. The KMT and its Republic of China government retreated to the island of Taiwan, from which Chiang planned to regroup and organize an attack to retake the mainland. Chiang made the strategic decision to hold on to three islands along the coast: Kinmen, Matsu, and Dachen. He believed keeping these footholds would offer a strategic advantage when launching an attack to retake China. As U.S. support for the Chinese Nationalists faded, this plan gradually became a pipe dream. Meanwhile, the forces of the newly founded People’s Republic of China constantly bombarded these islands with shells. Chiang eventually gave up Dachen, but held on to Kinmen and Matsu. An aerial photograph, taken from a plane, show Xiamen city (bottom), Little Kinmen (center) and Kinmen Island (left).

articles.title: The Hidden Famine: What I Saw in North Korea’s Darkest Years
articles.excerpt: “Miss Kathi: Saving Lives in North Korea” by Kathi Zellweger and Mike Chinoy chronicles the remarkable story of Kathi Zellweger, a native of Switzerland whose history of engagement with a secretive, isolated North Korea over nearly three decades is unprecedented in its scope, access, and humanitarian impact. It is one of the first book-length accounts in English by an aid worker operating on the ground in North Korea – the story of a woman who has lived out her commitment to the poor and most vulnerable undaunted by the tensions and threat of conflict perpetually looming over the Korean peninsula. For many North Koreans, Kathi was the first foreigner they had ever met or even seen. Playing a central role in the early years of international relief efforts in North Korea was a lonely job, as Kathi addressed the humanitarian needs of a suffering people largely ignored by the world because of their citizenship. She befriended local doctors, nurses, and caregivers; negotiated with suspicious government officials; overcame international doubts about the diversion of relief supplies to the military; and, over a period of years, spearheaded an effort that provided food, medicine, and development aid. Ultimately, her efforts saved the lives of thousands of people – most of them children. This excerpt from the book describes visits to people struggling to survive the famine in the northern city of Sinuiju. It was September 1998. I sat on the floor, Korean style, in Mrs. Kim’s apartment in Sinuiju, one of North Korea’s five largest cities. Located on the banks of the Yalu River just across from the Chinese town of Dandong, Sinuiju had been an important industrial center and a key transit point for trade with China before North Korea’s economy collapsed.

articles.title: A New Japanese Drydock and the Limits of Allied Cooperation
articles.excerpt: On August 19, Nikkei Asia reported that Namura Shipbuilding was planning to construct a new drydock for large vessel construction by 2035. Japan is already the third-largest shipbuilder in the world, and the expansion carries significant security and economic implications for the region. It follows a renewed commitment by Japan to invest in the shipbuilding sector, amidst growing security concerns around lackluster U.S. capacity and the role allies like Japan can play in filling security gaps. Yet the announcement highlights a more sobering reality regarding those prospects. Japanese shipyards are expanding because their current capacity is fully maxed out. Consequently, scaling future alliance cooperation may depend far less on reaching formal agreements than on securing available schedule space. The new drydock would be located in Imari Bay, on the northwestern coast of Kyushu in Saga prefecture, and would be the first new large drydock in Japan since 2017. Upon completion, it will reportedly focus on construction of liquefied natural gas carriers. The project follows a string of announcements from both the Japanese government and industry aimed at bolstering the sector. In November 2025, Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae designated 17 nationally important sectors – including shipbuilding – as sources of economic growth through public-private investments. The Japanese shipbuilding industry shared this ambition, outlining a roadmap aimed at doubling annual shipbuilding capacity to 18 million gross tons by around 2035. Both Japan’s government and industry are aiming to establish a 1 trillion yen ($6.5 billion) fund aimed at reviving Japanese shipbuilding. This slew of investments is motivated by multiple factors. For one, the shipbuilding sector was an important driver of Japanese economic growth and industrialization in the post-World War II period.

articles.title: Can Bangladesh Engage the Arakan Army Without Compromising Rohingya Rights?
articles.excerpt: Bangladesh is reportedly considering a dialogue between the Myanmar government and the Arakan Army, with a view to facilitating the repatriation of the 1 million Rohingya refugees currently living in Bangladesh. As the Arakan Army occupies significant territory in Rakhine State, there is a real need for effective communication. But communication based on the need of the moment should not be interpreted as political trust, recognition, or partnership. Will engagement with the Arakan Army ensure that Rohingya rights will be safeguarded – or little by little legitimize an armed authority that has allegedly committed serious abuses to the very people Bangladesh is trying to send back? The Myanmar military is responsible for the atrocities that occurred in 2017, including killings, mass rape, destruction of villages, and forced displacement. However, the Rohingya community has not been made safe by the end of the military rule in some areas of Rakhine. Instead the actions of the new rulers have caused serious concerns. The United Nations and Human Rights Watch have accused the Arakan Army of arbitrary detention, enforced disappearance, forced recruitment, forced labor, extortion, property seizure, and restrictions on movement and employment. The Arakan Army has also faced criticism for its failure to accept the Rohingya’s self-identification and its exclusionary attitude toward them. More seriously, the Arakan Army has been accused of attacking Rohingya civilians in the recent conflict. In May 2024, Human Rights Watch reported incidents of civilians being killed and wounded and of homes being destroyed in Hoyyar Siri village in Buthidaung Township. Some of the alleged abuses may be considered war crimes, the organization said. The Arakan Army has claimed that it was not responsible, yet survivors are still missing from their homes and being denied justice. These reports establish a basic conundrum for any plan of repatriation.

articles.title: How Mongolia Is Diversifying Its Defense Sector
articles.excerpt: This year, Turkiye and Mongolia launched the country’s first ammunition factory, marking an elevation in bilateral relations but also jumpstarting Mongolia’s defense manufacturing capabilities. It’s part of a larger trend: in the last decade, Mongolia’s defense sector has diversified immensely. Mongolia and Turkiye established a strategic partnership in January 2025 during Mongolian President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa’s state visit to Ankara. That was followed by several high-level visits by Turkish officials. In October 2025, Turkish Minister of National Defense Yasar Guler paid an official visit to Ulaanbaatar at the invitation of his Mongolian counterpart, Batlut Damba. The two sides discussed opportunities to deepen cooperation in military education, training, and officer exchange programs. During the same visit, Guler also participated in the inauguration of the new ammunition factory’s production line. The Mechanical and Chemical Industry Corporation, or MKE, a state-owned Turkish defense company, had signed a formal contract with Mongolia’s Defense Industrial Corporation in 2024 to establish a local ammunition production line in Mongolia. It’s MKE’s second overseas facility, following a production line in Jordan – and perhaps, more importantly, Mongolia’s first domestic ammunition factory. In August 2026, Mongolia announced that the MKE factory had officially begun production. In an interview, Batlut stated that Mongolia has now produced three types of ammunition. The government isn’t done yet; it is now looking to establish a drone factory as well. Turkiye has long been a reliable defense partner for Mongolia. Under a 1999 agreement, Ankara provides annual grants of $1 million to Mongolia’s defense sector. The two countries regularly exchange visits and hold training of military personnel. Turkiye is also an active participant in the Khaan Quest international military exercise, which is held annually in Mongolia.

articles.title: China’s Own Version of Ambiguity in the Taiwan Strait
articles.excerpt: Taipei spent 10 days in August rehearsing a war with Beijing. Its annual Han Kuang exercise in 2026 simulated a blockade, attacks on critical infrastructure, disrupted internet, and the transition from peacetime to full-scale conflict. But this time, Beijing waited until the final day to issue its first official comment, dismissing the drills as a “wasteful charade.” Beijing, in fact, appears to be cultivating a new form of “ambiguity” of its own. The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) remains active around Taiwan, but the balance of pressure has begun to look different. Compared with the dramatic encirclement exercises and large-scale military displays of recent years, Beijing’s military profile has been somewhat less conspicuous. Whether this reflects a deliberate signaling strategy cannot be established from open sources, but the broader pattern is obvious: in the first half of 2026, PLA fighter-jet activity around Taiwan fell to a three-year low. That decline sits uneasily with the conventional assumption that Beijing is steadily escalating military preparations for reunification. It suggests, instead, that China may be shifting part of its pressure campaign away from highly visible military coercion toward methods that are less easily classified. For example, while fighter jet numbers dropped, Taipei recorded 55 sightings of mainland Chinese government vessels around the island in June, including coast guard and research ships. That was 83 percent more than in May and 120 percent more than a year earlier. China has also begun coast guard patrols east of Taiwan, describing them not as military operations but as “routine law-enforcement patrols” in waters under Chinese jurisdiction. In other words, Beijing is not necessarily reducing pressure; it is changing its form. Gray-zone activities blur the line between military coercion and civilian enforcement. This creates an emerging paradox in the Taiwan Strait.

articles.title: Australia and Thailand Deepen Ties to Hedge Against Global Uncertainty
articles.excerpt: In recent months, the Australia government has been incredibly active on the diplomatic front, from new security agreements with multiple Pacific Island countries to visits to Australia by the Japanese, Indian, New Zealand, and Vietnamese leaders. This week Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul made his way to Australia. For both Canberra and Bangkok, there is a desire to build more substantive regional relationships as a hedge against both a more unreliable Washington and a more assertive Beijing – as well as buttress against the rippling effects of the competition between the two superpowers. The Australia-Thailand relationship is therefore less about alliance-building than about building greater resilience through diversifying partnerships, and creating a latticework of cooperation within the Indo-Pacific region. The two prime ministers signed a series of agreements during Anutin’s visit that sought to give this strategy practical substance. These included deepening cooperation on transnational crime, including online scams, cybercrime, money laundering, human trafficking, and narcotics. The purpose of these agreements is to enable greater information sharing and coordination between the two countries’ law enforcement agencies. Alongside this, the prime ministers committed to deepening economic engagement. Since the signing of the Thailand-Australia Free Trade Agreement in 2005, trade between the two countries has tripled, with Thailand becoming Australia’s fifth largest source of imports. But both countries believe there is room for expansion. They highlighted that cooperation across agriculture, clean energy, education, healthcare, critical technologies, resources, creative industries, and the digital economy were areas of greater ambition. The other major announcement was the establishment of a biennial defense ministers’ meeting. The two countries have had a longstanding, but low-key, defense relationship.

articles.title: How an Academic Became Collateral Damage to China’s Interests in Myanmar
articles.excerpt: On June 3, Burmese-American scholar U Min Zin disappeared in China’s southwestern province of Yunnan, where he was set to attend an academic conference. On June 12, shortly before Myanmar’s ruler, Min Aung Hlaing, arrived in China for a state visit, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian confirmed that Zin had been arrested and accused of endangering Chinese national security. No further details were provided. On August 20, the U.S. State Department officially classified Zin as “wrongfully detained.” Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs Dylan Johnson pledged that the U.S. government “will continue to advocate for Mr. Zin and call for the release of all U.S. citizens who are arbitrarily detained or exit banned in China.” Zin runs the Institute for Strategy and Policy-Myanmar, a think tank in Thailand that is critical of Myanmar’s military government and the 2021 coup that brought it to power. Initially, the arrest of Zin, a U.S. citizen, may seem like another attempt by Beijing to engage in hostage diplomacy and gain the upper hand in any potential negotiations with the United States at the September summit between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. But Beijing’s arrest of Zin actually has more to do with Myanmar itself. China wanted to remove a potentially destabilizing variable from the already unsteady foundations of Chinese investment in Myanmar, which is key to Beijing’s economic strategy in Southeast Asia. For China, its core strategic interests in Myanmar are the stability of its shared border, the safety of its economic investments, and the closure of scam centers that ensnare and enslave Chinese nationals. To that end, Beijing supports the military junta that seized power from Myanmar’s democratically elected government. China has provided the new regime with $3 billion in economic assistance, as well as selling it military weapons. Beijing also applies diplomatic pressure on Myanmar’s ethnic armed organizations.

articles.title: Is Pakistan’s Province Debate a Political Gimmick?
articles.excerpt: From time to time, the debate over creating new provinces arises in Pakistani politics. This debate receives attention in the media for a while, only to fade away after some time as if it never existed. Consequently, the airtime for proponents of new provinces disappears as well. Some view this debate as a political gimmick designed to distract the public from the real issues facing the country, while others believe that influential figures operate behind the scenes to extract concessions from those in political power by stirring up this debate. It is indeed possible for a select few to hold power while others manipulate events from the sidelines in a hybrid democracy like Pakistan, which has experienced dictatorial rule for 34 of its 79 years of existence since 1947. The debate of dividing the existing four provinces of Pakistan and creating new provinces has resurfaced once again after a statement made by Pakistani Interior and Narcotics Control Minister Mohsin Naqvi late last month. While addressing the first Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad, he said: The system we are living under has collapsed. You have been dragging this system for 70 years, and while we all want democracy, there are many forms within democracy. Problems cannot be solved through the current dispensation. If this system continues, we will still be sitting here a decade from now discussing the same issues. The only solution is to take [the matter of] administrative units, provinces or whatever you may call it, to the public. These remarks by a minister caused an uproar across the country, with some in favor of creating new provinces and other against. The minister’s own colleagues, including Defense Minister Khawaja Asif and Prime Minister’s Advisor on Political and Public Affairs Rana Sanaullah, have not shown any particular support for the notion. Sanaullah said the government has no plan at present regarding new provinces.

articles.title: Nepal’s Tibet Conference Controversy Is About More Than Chinese Pressure
articles.excerpt: The cancellation of the in-person 17th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (IATS), scheduled for Kathmandu from August 23-29, is being portrayed in Nepal and abroad as the country caving in to China’s undue pressure. That is not wrong — but it is an incomplete analysis. The cancellation also reflects the Nepal government’s troubled ties with Beijing, inadequate diplomatic outreach, and, just as importantly, the Nepali state’s lack of confidence in its ability to manage politically sensitive events. The government of Balendra Shah, Nepal’s current prime minister and senior leader of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), got off on the wrong foot with China. The September 2025 Gen Z uprising, which overthrew the K.P. Sharma Oli government and cleared the way for the RSP’s rise to power, saw the participation of some youths wearing clothes with the insignia of “TOB.” According to a popular narrative, the acronym stood for “Tibetan Original Bloodline.” Its members supposedly wanted to “hijack” the movement for the “Free Tibet” cause. Though there was no hard evidence to establish this link, the narrative gained traction in pro-Beijing circles. So did the related speculation that the Gen Z protests were the handiwork of Western spy agencies. Then there is Sudan Gurung. The current Nepali home minister has been persistently linked to the Free Tibet movement and the alleged TOB protestors. There were still other reasons for China to doubt the Shah government’s adherence to the “One China” policy. In a rare move, the Dalai Lama had congratulated the erstwhile government of Sushila Karki, the ex-chief justice who had been picked by Shah to lead the interim government formed after the Gen Z uprising. Then, when Shah became the prime minister after the March 2026 elections, the head of the Tibetan government-in-exile officially extended his good wishes.

articles.title: Singapore Needs a Broader Conversation About How to Measure Economic Progress
articles.excerpt: Singapore turned 61 last weekend. Approaching this milestone has led to some existential discussions: the world around Singapore is changing, what worked before has been plunged into question, and its identity and strengths are being re-examined. That the global economy is witnessing a confluence of geopolitical risks, unprecedented technological advancement and a rewiring of the global order prompted Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to convene an Economic Strategy Review (ESR) exercise earlier in the year helmed by some of his younger and newer political colleagues. However, that did not stop Singapore’s Parliament from holding a marathon robust debate on its economic strategies in the same week as its National Day celebrations, prompted by a motion proposed by the opposition Workers’ Party. By and large, it was a healthy and positive exercise, especially when the premise of the debate was to evaluate if the country’s economic growth has benefited, and will continue to benefit, Singaporeans. The ESR itself had noted the structural changes that the global and domestic economies were facing: geopolitical fragmentation, AI and automation, slower workforce growth, ageing, intensifying competition for investment, changing employment patterns, and concerns over inequality and mobility – and suggested strategies to address them. Further, Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry also expects the nation’s annual growth to slow down to 2-3 percent over the next decade, noting that sustaining growth and creating good jobs will become more difficult as time goes by. Singapore Should Not Apologize For Being an Open Economy Hence, it was entirely appropriate and fitting for the country’s legislative body to question and debate if and how Singapore’s economic model should evolve.

articles.title: The Last Breath of Rayong
articles.excerpt: Fisherfolk in Thailand’s Rayong province are currently facing multiple impacts from industrial expansion in the region – in particular, the construction of a MapTaPhut Phase 3 port and the development of large-scale investment projects including liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects, including LNG terminal and regasification facilities. The expansion of LNG projects in the eastern provinces, part of Thailand’s plan to position itself as a regional LNG hub, has disturbed and now threatens to destroy the coastal fisheries resources that communities have long relied on. “We used to fish regularly, and we are at ease earning money from fishing,” one fisherman in the Klonglawon community of Rayong province told researchers in 2025. “Now the seas are changing tremendously due to industrialization and its expansion, with seas filling and other so-called ‘development’ projects. Fish are reducing, and our livelihoods are at the front lines. It will never be the same without rehabilitation.” Fisherfolk in Rayong are now demanding compensation for the loss of fisheries and livelihoods. The injustice associated with LNG development is not limited to environmental impacts but is fundamentally tied to unequal power structures in which affected communities have little influence over decisions that shape their future. Thailand is heavily reliant on fossil fuels, and particularly natural gas, to drive the country’s economic growth and industrialization. According to data from Thailand’s Energy Regulatory Commission, natural gas accounts for 58 percent of Thailand’s power generation mix, followed by electricity imports from Laos (14 percent), coal (13 percent), and renewables (12 percent). Natural gas remains the backbone of power generation, sourced from both the Gulf of Thailand and LNG imported from abroad.

articles.title: What Asia’s Industrialization Lessons Can Teach Fragmented States
articles.excerpt: When Asia’s economic transformation is discussed, the focus usually falls on the spectacular numbers: China’s rise to become the world’s manufacturing center, South Korea’s emergence as an industrial and technology powerhouse, or Vietnam’s more recent transformation into a major manufacturing base. Less attention is paid to the infrastructure of interdependence that made this transformation possible. Over several decades, factories, ports, roads, financial institutions and supply chains became connected across national borders, creating an economic geography that was far more integrated than the fragmented political map. Delving into the question of why is very telling. Asia did not become integrated because its governments necessarily saw eye to eye on regional matters. China and Japan remain, as ever, strategic competitors, India and China continue to face serious tensions, while Southeast Asia more broadly is awash with countries that each hold different strategic interests as top priority, alongside of course, varying political systems. Despite this, economic integration has continued. The Asian Development Bank’s 2026 assessment identified trade as the strongest driver of regional integration, while cross-border investment and production networks continue to deepen economic links across Asia and the Pacific. The ADB also noted that Asia’s trade connections remain predominantly intraregional, reflecting deep and sustained commercial ties. The consequence is that political uncertainty or disruption increasingly carries a firm economic cost. That is particularly visible when supply chains are disrupted or trade policy changes abruptly. Economic prosperity requires policy stability, just as manufacturers need functioning ports and reliable energy and exporters need predictable access to markets. The more interconnected economies become, the more constituencies emerge with an interest in maintaining those connections.

articles.title: Vietnam Proposes Ending Death Penalty For 6 More Offenses
articles.excerpt: ⁠Vietnam’s government has proposed a further narrowing of its use of the death penalty, part of a broad overhaul of its Penal Code that could also see the authorities increase punishments for “anti-state” acts. A draft revision of the Code presented to the National Assembly yesterday proposed removing the death penalty for an additional six offences, including drug trafficking, the rape of minors, crimes against humanity, and war crimes, state media reported. If approved, the revision would leave the death penalty in place for just four crimes: treason, murder, terrorism, and the illegal production of narcotics. The National Assembly is expected to debate the revisions in the coming weeks before voting on them in October. The move comes after Vietnam last year removed the death penalty for eight criminal offenses, including embezzlement, bribe taking, espionage, illegally transporting narcotics, sabotaging state infrastructure, and “crime aimed at overthrowing the people’s government.” These changes spared the life of real estate tycoon Truong My Lan, who was sentenced to death in 2024 for her role in a $12 billion corruption scandal. The maximum sentence for all of these crimes is now life imprisonment. Over the past four decades, Vietnam’s government has gradually reduced the scope of capital punishment. In the 1985 Penal Code, the death penalty applied to 44 offenses, Tuoi Tre reported last week. This dropped to 29 in the 1999 Code, 22 in the 2009 Code, 18 in the 2015 Code, and 10 under the current version, which took effect on July 1, 2025. Last year, Minister of Justice Nguyen Hai Ninh said that the decision to reduce the use of the death penalty “was based on careful analysis of the nature and severity of the offenses, the value of the interests protected, and the potential for remedying the harm caused.” The narrowing of the use of capital punishment is part of a wider legal reform effort that could affect hundreds of provisions of Vietnam’s Penal Code.

articles.title: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir Elected Bangladesh’s New President
articles.excerpt: The Pulse | Politics | South Asia The presidential election has reopened debate over Article 70 of the Constitution, which can cost parliamentarians their seats if they vote against their party. Veteran Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected Bangladesh’s new president on August 20. It was the country’s first contested presidential election since 1991. Since then, presidential candidates had been elected unopposed, with no rival entering the race. Alamgir, 78, received 255 votes in Parliament. His rival, Liberal Democratic Party chairman Oli Ahmad, won 88. Ahmad was backed by an 11-party opposition alliance led by the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami (JI). The vote came less than a month after former President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned on July 24. Shahabuddin cited serious health problems, but his departure also followed sustained political pressure. Shahabuddin was elected in 2023 with the backing of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League. After Hasina’s government fell in August 2024, several political groups and student leaders called for him to step down. Shahabuddin denied that he had stepped down under pressure The presidential election also reopened debate over Article 70 of the Constitution, which states that parliamentarians can lose their seats if they vote against their party. JI leaders argued that the provision prevented MPs from voting freely and called for its reform before the election. A Supreme Court lawyer challenged the provision and asked the High Court to suspend the presidential election. He argued that MPs should be able to vote independently. The High Court rejected the petition on August 18, clearing the way for the election. Alamgir had served as BNP secretary-general since 2016. He became one of the party’s most recognizable faces during its long years in opposition under Hasina.

articles.title: Ahead of Xi Visit, US Designates American Held in China as ‘Wrongfully Detained’
articles.excerpt: The U.S. State Department yesterday designated Myanmar scholar and U.S. citizen Min Zin as “wrongfully detained,” two months after his arrest in China on espionage charges. The move was announced by Dylan Johnson, assistant secretary of state for global public affairs, who said that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had made the designation after “an extensive review of the circumstances” surrounding Min Zin’s arrest on June 3. “The safety and security of U.S. citizens is the State Department’s top priority,” Johnson said. “We will continue to advocate for Mr. Zin and call for the release of all U.S. citizens who are arbitrarily detained or exit banned in China.” The announcement follows a report by Reuters news agency about the designation, which cited a senior State Department official. The State Department said that Min Zin is the second American who is wrongfully detained in China after Youlin Chen, a Chinese-born American seismologist from Boston who has published U.S.-funded work on North Korean nuclear tests. He was arrested in November 2024 and designated wrongfully detained by Rubio in March. Min Zin, the executive director of the Institute for Strategy and Policy-Myanmar (ISP-Myanmar), disappeared on June 3 while visiting the city of Kunming in Yunnan province for a conference. A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson confirmed his arrest a week later, stating that Min Zin, a former student activist who participated in pro-democracy protests in 1988, had “been placed under criminal detention by the ​relevant authorities in accordance with the law on suspicion of engaging in espionage and ​endangering China’s national security.” The senior State Department official told Reuters that Min Zin was detained inside the airport and has been “subjected to repeated interrogations, isolation and detention conditions” for nearly 11 weeks.

articles.title: China Isn’t Winning the Digital Order – Yet
articles.excerpt: Across Southeast Asia, Chinese firms have laid fiber-optic cable, built smart-city platforms, supplied 5G networks, and even donated laptops to defense ministries. By one common account in Washington, this is what losing looks like: through its Digital Silk Road, Beijing is exporting not just technology but authoritarianism itself. But ask the officials who actually regulate these systems what rules they follow, and a more complicated picture emerges. Indonesia’s cybersecurity agencies enforce technical standards developed in Geneva. The Philippines modeled its data privacy law on European regulation. Malaysia’s approach to artificial intelligence borrows from U.N. principles and regional frameworks. In three of the Digital Silk Road’s most important partner countries, Chinese hardware is widespread but Chinese rules are not. China may be winning many of the contracts to build out Southeast Asia’s digital infrastructure, but Beijing is making less headway on the rules. Understanding this – and the factors behind this reality – complicates the prevailing concern about digital authoritarianism. However, there is one scenario in which the hand-wringing about digital authoritarianism could become a self-fulfilling prophecy. China’s Digital Silk Road China’s Digital Silk Road (DSR), the technological arm of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), has spread Chinese-built networks, surveillance systems, and cloud infrastructure across the developing world. Embedded in that infrastructure, many argue, is a political model: “cyber sovereignty,” centralized data control, and a state’s right to intervene in its digital sphere as it sees fit. Analysts have warned that the world could fragment into technological spheres of influence, and Southeast Asia – a region that is young, rapidly digitalizing, and ambivalent about democracy – is seen as fertile soil for Beijing’s model. These concerns are legitimate and deserve to be taken seriously.

articles.title: ROK-US Alliance Management Via Social Media
articles.excerpt: Asia Geopolitics | Security | East Asia A line-by-line analysis of U.S. President Donald Trump’s surprising (?) social media post downsizing the ongoing South Korea-U.S. military exercises at the very last minute. U.S. President Donald Trump’s other August 17 social media post. Credit: Truth Social / @realDonaldTrump In the latest episode of The Diplomat’s Asia Geopolitics podcast, hosts Katie Putz and Ankit Panda do a line-by-line analysis of U.S. President Donald Trump’s surprising (?) social media post downsizing the ongoing South Korea-U.S. military exercises at the very last minute. They dig into the roots of each sentence and their implications for the South Korea-U.S. alliance and the potential for future talks between the U.S. and North Korea. You can subscribe to The Diplomat’s Asia Geopolitics podcast on Apple Podcasts and Spotify; and watch the episode on YouTube. AuthorsStaff AuthorAnkit PandaAnkit Panda is editor-at-large at The Diplomat and the Stanton Senior Fellow in the Nuclear Policy Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Follow him on Twitter.View ProfileStaff AuthorCatherine PutzCatherine Putz is managing editor of The Diplomat.View ProfileTagsAsia GeopoliticsSecurityEast AsiaNorth KoreaSouth KoreaUnited StatesTrump alliancesTrump North Korea policyU.S.-South Korea allianceU.S.-South Korea military exercisesUlchi Freedom Shield

articles.title: What Are the Implications of the Mecca Pact for India?
articles.excerpt: The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkiye, signed on August 7, evoked both disconcertion and skepticism in New Delhi’s strategic circles. The official reaction, delivered by the spokesperson of India’s External Affairs Ministry, to the sudden unveiling of what is being increasingly referred to as an “Islamic NATO” was one of quiet concern. The spokesperson observed that the Indian government – in a typical diplomatic aphorism that gives little away – is “examining its implications” from the perspective of “our national security” and “regional peace and stability.” He said that India would “safeguard its national interests.” Still, most of the country’s strategic community was more openly alarmed. Although many have dismissed the agreement as more optics than substance, the pact is seen by some as a master stroke by Pakistan, India’s arch-rival. It may be time for New Delhi to recalibrate its approach to the Gulf, a region of immense economic and strategic importance. Approximately 8.8 million Indian nationals reside in the region. The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) is India’s largest regional-bloc trading partner, comprising 15.4 percent of India’s total trade. India and the GCC signed a free trade agreement in February this year. While the fine print of the Mecca agreement has yet to surface and its practical implications not yet worked out, the pact envisages bringing together three countries – a GCC member, a NATO member, and a South Asian country that happens to be the only Islamic nuclear power – under a collective deterrence mechanism. The aggregate matrix of all three countries, according to the Global Firepower Index (GFI) 2026 that evaluates 145 modern military entities, could produce a significant fielding of military might, consisting of 1.4 million active personnel, more than 6,000 tanks, 3,415 military aircraft, 844 naval assets, and defense spending of more than $124 billion.

articles.title: A 4,000‑yr‑old Rock Painting in Indonesia Offers Clues to One of Humanity’s Greatest Migrations
articles.excerpt: Some 4,200 years ago, people started to leave what is now Taiwan to migrate to the thousands of islands to the south, spanning as far west as Madagascar in the western Indian Ocean and as far east as Rapa Nui (Easter Island) in the eastern Pacific Ocean. We can trace this migration through the way language spread, creating the largest-scale language dispersal in prehistory. But what exactly drove these people to make these distant and dangerous voyages? Our discovery of a 4,000-year-old painting of a sunburst in southeastern Indonesia offers some clues. Austronesian is a close-knit language family spoken across much of Malaysia, the Philippines, Indonesia, Madagascar, and the Pacific Islands. Some of the major languages in this family include Malay, Javanese, Sundanese, Tagalog, Cebuano and Malagasy. We know the Austronesian migration began at least around 4,200 years ago, as this is when characteristic Austronesian red pottery and rectangular stone adzes (axe-like tools) appear on islands south of Taiwan. The extraordinary seafaring abilities of Austronesians were underpinned by the outrigger canoe, but it is unclear which other factors propelled their expansion. Previous models have suggested advancements in rice farming and storage (thanks to pottery) might have fueled population growth, prompting the Austronesian people to migrate to neighboring islands for new farmland. However, rice and pottery are not universal features of Austronesian societies. An alternative theory is that there was a powerful and charismatic cultural identity shared by the Austronesian people – the kind that attracted outsiders and encouraged daring voyages to remote uninhabited islands. Finding archaeological evidence for the presence of a past cultural identity is difficult, but rock art does provide a way.

articles.title: Why the World’s Hedging Responses to China’s Rare Earth Dominance Have Failed
articles.excerpt: China’s dominance over the global supply of rare earth minerals – and related export controls – have been one of Beijing’s key geoeconomic levers in recent years. Since the second wave of U.S. trade sanctions in April 2025, China has ramped up restrictions. Most recently, in June 2026, Beijing added more new U.S. companies and created a reporting mechanism for violations, thereby further weaponizing its rare earths dominance. Government efforts to diversify away from China in Asia, North America, and Europe have been moderately successful, foremost regarding light rare earths. But Beijing still possesses such extraordinary leverage, particularly in the heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). These materials are essential in the production of high-temperature permanent magnets and are widely used in advanced defense systems, electric vehicles, and offshore wind turbines. It is evident China is the lone superpower in this field. It currently dominates all three stages of the value chain, with International Energy Agency (IEA) statistics showing China controls nearly 60 percent of HREE mining, 91 percent of refining, and 94 percent of magnet production in 2024. Notably, China’s dominance increases as it moves downstream. China has the world’s largest reserves of rare earths, with nearly 44 million metric tons, nearly 48 percent of global reserves, according to the USGS. But that’s only part of the story. China’s main advantage lies in the refining and production stages that turn rare earths in usable inputs. This is the result of decades of investment in perfecting the technical know-how and the supporting ecosystem that cannot be simply replaced. Recreating China’s supply chain is therefore not a resource issue, but an expertise and ecosystem one. There is no single competitor that currently possesses China’s combination of resources, processing capacity, technical expertise, manufacturing scale, and downstream demand.

articles.title: After 9 Years, China Is Reopening Its Borders To Recycled Plastic
articles.excerpt: In November 2026, the European Union will prohibit exports of potentially recyclable plastic to non-OECD countries. The EU labeled these exports “waste” and described the cross-border flows as “environmental exploitation.” At the same time that the EU is shutting down the trade, China has reversed course and committed to expanding the movement of recyclable plastic across its border. For most of the past decade, China was closed to imports of plastic waste entirely. The EU and China seem to be moving in different directions. Europe’s efforts concentrate on boosting demand for recycled plastic at home while taking a hardline position on exports abroad. China’s new approach is centered on supply and weaker on the demand for recycled plastic. Each holds lessons for the other, because a scalable framework for tackling global plastic pollution requires action on both the demand and supply sides. And yet the recent developments in China have drawn almost no analysis outside China. That’s a mistake, because no country in recent history has shaped the global recycling trade more than China. China’s Plastic Ban China’s “National Sword” policy, launched in 2017, abruptly closed the country to imports of plastic waste – a seachange for China, which had absorbed much of the world’s recovered plastic for two decades. There were good reasons for the change. Much of the plastic waste wealthier countries shipped to China was contaminated or unrecyclable, local importers often lacked the capacity to handle it, and China’s monitoring system was underdeveloped at the time. The result was increased plastic pollution inside China. The National Sword program curbed the air and land pollution that earlier shipments had caused and forced a reckoning in countries that had outsourced their waste sorting problem for a generation. However, National Sword, on its own, could not build a circular economy for plastic.

articles.title: North Korea Dismisses Trump’s Recent Overtures to Kim Jong Un
articles.excerpt: Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said there was no communication between the leaders of the United States and North Korea, according to a statement published by the North’s state-controlled Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on August 19. “As for the news from Washington that shortly ago, there was a communication between the leaders of the DPRK and the U.S., I am not aware of it at all, and perhaps it may be the only thing I do not know as regards the foreign policy of our supreme leadership,” Kim said. (DPRK is an acronym of North Korea’s official name, Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.) It was the first response of Pyongyang to U.S. President Donald Trump’s claim that Kim Jong Un responded to his overtures. According to the Wall Street Journal, Trump has discussed setting up a meeting with Kim Jong Un on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which will be held in November in Shenzhen, China. In the past few days, Trump has made friendly gestures to Kim Jong Un. He posted a photo of him and Kim taking a stroll during the Hanoi Summit in 2019 and a meme of Kim making a phone call, with text suggesting he was calling Trump. On August 17, Trump said on his Truth Social account that he had ordered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to “substantially reduce” the joint military exercises with South Korea, which began on the same day. The Ulchi Freedom Shield joint military exercises were supposed to last until August 27 but, according to local media reports, they will end on August 21. South Korea’s Foreign Affairs and Defense Ministries said on August 19 that Washington had not explained or given advance notice regarding Trump’s decision to scale down the joint military exercises. However, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung showed a positive attitude, saying that he will remain fully dedicated to serving as “a peacemaker” to facilitate and contribute to Trump’s peacemaking endeavors.

articles.title: Dr. Moses Haregewoyn and the Operational Case for a Different Kind of Global Health Leadership
articles.excerpt: When governments lose the ability to administer healthcare access, they do not announce it. There is no declaration, no visible collapse. What happens instead is quieter and more corrosive: eligible citizens fall through eligibility systems, enrollment backlogs accumulate, coverage lapses at moments of medical need, and the public health framework that policy makers spent years designing begins to fail the people it was built for — not because the policy was wrong, but because no one built the infrastructure to carry it. This is the governance failure that rarely appears in international health leadership discourse. And it is the failure that Dr. Moses Haregewoyn has spent more than three decades working to prevent. As President of Automated Health Systems, Dr. Haregewoyn leads an organization that functions as an operational layer of public health access across the United States. AHS does not provide medical treatment; it does something that health systems increasingly depend on but rarely discuss: it ensures that the administrative architecture connecting citizens to coverage actually works. Eligibility determination, enrollment brokerage, managed care coordination, citizen support infrastructure — these are the systems through which healthcare policy either reaches people or fails to. AHS operates in that space, at national scale, in partnership with government agencies across effectively all fifty states. The Strategic Dimension of Health Administration The COVID-19 pandemic clarified something that public health analysts had long argued without sufficient audience: health system capacity is not a social welfare metric. It is a component of national resilience. States that could not administer coverage, manage redeterminations at scale, or maintain contact center operations under surge conditions did not merely fail their citizens medically.

articles.title: Can Japan Become Indonesia’s Principal Partner in Asia?
articles.excerpt: Japan is increasingly positioning itself to become Indonesia’s primary strategic partner in the Indo-Pacific region. Over the past 12 months, the two nations have substantially deepened bilateral cooperation in defense and energy, among other long-term strategic sectors beyond trade and investment. As strategic competition intensifies throughout Southeast Asia, Indonesia is seeking partners that can strengthen its security and economy while respecting its non-aligned foreign policy. Meanwhile, Japan is seeking to take on an expanded role as a regional security provider that complements its existing economic presence in Southeast Asia. Put together, these converging interests highlight how the Indonesia-Japan relationship is entering a new phase defined by long-term strategic partnership. The strategic interests of both Indonesia and Japan complement each other well. Indonesia’s current status as Southeast Asia’s largest economy, its control over the Malacca, Sunda, Lombok, and Makassar straits, and its abundant natural resources all synergize well with Japan’s expertise in defense, manufacturing, and emerging technologies. However, this growing relationship faces a variety of challenges on both sides. Political uncertainty in both countries, including declining approval ratings for Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae, economic uncertainty in Indonesia, and the arrest of Indonesia’s top anti-corruption prosecutor, could complicate long-term policymaking. Public opinion also poses a challenge, with some Indonesians having seen Japan as being too closely aligned with the United States. This raises questions about whether deeper cooperation between Indonesia and Japan is compatible with Indonesia’s long-standing non-aligned foreign policy. For Japan to become Indonesia’s principal Asian partner, Tokyo must demonstrate that increased cooperation strengthens Indonesia’s national sovereignty and strategic flexibility.

articles.title: China Praises Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim For Supportive Comments on Taiwan
articles.excerpt: China has praised recent comments by Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, in which he described Taiwan as a province of China and expressed support for its use of force in the pursuit of national “reunification.” In an interview with Al Jazeera published on Sunday, the Malaysian leader said that he saw “Taiwan as part of China, period.” He added that there was “one China” and that this was “accepted by all.” Anwar also expressed support for China’s right to use force in order to unify the country, arguing that if a province of Malaysia attempted to secede, it would be his responsibility to “protect the sanctity and unity of the nation” – by force if necessary. “China appreciates the remarks by Prime Minister Anwar,” China’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said at a daily press briefing in Beijing yesterday. “I would like to reiterate that there’s only one China in the world. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory, and China must and will be reunited.” Anwar’s comments caused a conversely negative reaction in Taipei, where the Taiwanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Tuesday that Anwar’s “one-sided support for China could negatively impact Taiwanese businesses’ confidence in investing in Malaysia.” His apparent support for unilateral efforts to change the status quo in the Taiwan Strait via the threat of force “severely damages political trust between Taiwan and Malaysia.” The ministry also said that if Malaysia’s leader was really a defender of human rights, as he has long claimed, he should “uphold universal values such as democracy, freedom, human rights, and the rule of law, and respect the will of the people.” The standoff reflects the difficulties that Malaysia has faced in its attempt to maintain a balance between. Malaysia remains economically close to China, but has also welcomed investment from other Asian countries, including Taiwan – including in the country’s high-tech industry.

articles.title: Myanmar Military Chief Begins Visit to Thailand Aimed at Expanding Security Ties
articles.excerpt: The commander-in-chief of Myanmar’s armed forces arrived yesterday in Bangkok on an official visit aimed at expanding security cooperation between the two neighbors, two weeks after his predecessor, Min Aung Hlaing. The three-day visit by Ye Win Oo, Myanmar’s former spy chief, is the first that he has made since being appointed as military chief on March 30, and the latest in a string of diplomatic engagements between Bangkok and Naypyidaw. Ye Win Oo will attend a high-level meeting with Ukrit Boontanon, the commander-in-chief of the Royal Thai Armed Forces, and other high-ranking Thai military officers, the state-run Global New Light of Myanmar reported yesterday. These talks will focus “on matters related to bilateral relations and cooperation,” it added. The visit comes after Thailand hosted Ye Win Oo’s predecessor and mentor Min Aung Hlaing, who stepped down as military chief before being anointed president in April. Min Aung Hlaing held talks with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, who affirmed Thailand’s support for the normalization of Myanmar’s relations with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which has been in a state of suspended animation since shortly after the 2021 coup. In a joint statement, Bangkok “reaffirmed its commitment to supporting and continuing to work closely with Myanmar for Myanmar’s full and equal participation in ASEAN mechanisms and processes.” Myanmar in turn “expressed its appreciation for Thailand’s constructive role in facilitating the normalization of its relations with ASEAN.” All of this is part of Bangkok’s policy of “calibrated engagement” with Myanmar’s military-appointed government, which contends that the best way to manage the country’s conflicts is by bringing the country back into the “ASEAN family,” as Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow has put it.

articles.title: Kazakh State Tightens Grip Over Critical Minerals Miner ERG
articles.excerpt: On August 23, Kazakhstan will hold elections to its newly established unicameral parliament, the Kurultai, marking the latest phase of the political elite’s consolidation under President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Last month, the Constitutional Court determined that Tokayev can legally stand for the presidency again under the new basic law that entered force on July 1, leaving his earlier pledge not to seek office again – his current term ends in 2029 – firmly in the balance. Whether Tokayev decides to exercise that privilege or not, Kazakhstan’s business elite is being recast in his image, right in time for a new electoral cycle. Despite his criticisms of the “oligopolies” formed under predecessor Nursultan Nazarbayev, some of the country’s most powerful companies outside of the oil sector are now concentrated in even fewer hands, thanks to a series of megadeals first reported in the second half of last year. At the same time there has been a subtle shift, with the new captains of industry visibly more tethered to officialdom writ large than the Nazarbayev-loyal oligarchs who preceded them. One of the clearest examples of this trend is Luxembourg-domiciled Eurasian Resources Group (ERG), a mining group whose critical minerals output is globally significant, and whose contribution to the Kazakh economy is estimated between 2 and 4 percent of GDP. Integra, ERG, and Business ‘China-style’ In a series of clips posted to his official Instagram, Kudrat Shamiyev discusses Integra Construction KZ, “the biggest construction company in Kazakhstan,” with another delegate at an international Taekwondo event. “We do exchange… I own mining company. So, we take resources, we give enough,” begins Integra’s 36-year-old chairman, who is also Kazakhstan’s Taekwondo federation chief, speaking in English. The clip is backed by Drake’s 2023 track, featuring J. Cole, “First Person Shooter. “Similar to China-style?” interjects the man seen in the clip.

articles.title: Putin’s Visit to Disputed Island Exacerbates Japan-Russia Tensions
articles.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin visited Iturup Island (known in Japan as Etorofu) on August 13. It’s the largest of the disputed Southern Kurils, which are known as the Northern Territories in Japan. The islands have been occupied by Russia since the end of World War II but are also claimed by Japan. The Kuril Islands have been a constant thorn in Japan-Russia relations. The disputed islands are one of the reasons that Japan and Russia have yet to sign a peace treaty concluding World War II. Japan has long sought to foster economic cooperation with Russia as part of a broader push to normalize relations – and finally resolve the dispute. The Kuril Islands/Northern Territories issue was especially close to the heart of former Prime Minister Abe Shinzo, given its importance to his father, Abe Shintaro, during the elder Abe’s tenure as Japan’s foreign minister. However, the circumstances for Japan-Russia rapprochement are unfavorable. Since 2022, Japan has joined the United States and European states in condemning Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and imposing sanctions on Russia. After Japan imposed sanctions, Russia formally suspended peace treaty negotiations and canceled visa-free travel for Japanese nationals to visit ancestral graves on the disputed islands. Now Putin’s visit to one of the disputed islands has enflamed tensions still further. Then-President Dmitry Medvedev visited in 2010; however, this is the first time Putin has done so.

articles.title: Guinea: Mindestens 30 Tote nach Erdrutsch auf Müllkippe in Conakry
articles.excerpt: Beim Abrutschen einer Müllkippe auf ein Wohngebiet in Guinea sind mindestens 30 Menschen gestorben. Mindestens 22 weitere Menschen wurden bei dem Unglück verletzt, sechs von ihnen schwer, wie die Regierung des westafrikanischen Landes am Sonntagabend mitteilte. Die Suche nach möglichen Verschütteten sowie die Bergung von Leichen in dem Vorort Dar-es-Salam am Rande der Hauptstadt Conakry dauerten demnach an. Der Vorfall ereignete sich nach Regierungsangaben in der Nacht zum Sonntag. Die Müllkippe rutschte nach schweren Regenfällen ab und begrub eine angrenzende Siedlung unter sich. Tage zuvor hatte die Regierung eine Räumung des Gebiets und Sicherheitsmaßnahmen angeordnet, weil die Deponie instabil geworden war. Offenbar waren nicht alles Anwohner dieser Anordnung gefolgt.Der im Exil lebende Oppositionspolitiker und ehemalige Regierungschef Cellou Dalein Diallo erklärte im Onlinedienst Facebook, das Unglück sei »umso beunruhigender, als die Schließung der Deponie für diesen Sonntag« angekündigt worden war. Er forderte die Behörden auf, »in voller Transparenz die Umstände zu klären, die zu dieser Katastrophe geführt haben, und daraus sämtliche Konsequenzen zu ziehen«. Land ist reich an Rohstoffen – doch viele Menschen sind armDie Such- und Rettungsarbeiten dauerten weiter an. Premierminister Amadou Oury Bah besuchte den Unglücksort und sprach den Betroffenen im Namen der Regierung sein Beileid aus. Im Viertel Dar-es-Salam, einer der ärmsten Gegenden von Conakry, war es bereits 2017 zu einem Erdrutsch mit zahlreichen Todesopfern gekommen.Guinea gehört trotz großen Rohstoffreichtums zu den ärmsten Staaten der Welt. Das westafrikanische Land mit rund 15 Millionen Einwohnern zählt zu den weltweit wichtigsten Exporteuren von Bauxit, dem wichtigsten Ausgangsstoff für Aluminium. Viele Menschen haben trotzdem nur unzureichenden Zugang zu Gesundheitsversorgung, Bildung, Strom und sauberem Trinkwasser.
articles.summary: 几内亚首都科纳克里郊区的达尔萨拉姆（Dar-es-Salam）社区发生垃圾填埋场滑坡事故，掩埋了附近的居民区，造成至少30人死亡，至少22人受伤，其中6人伤势严重。西非国家政府周日晚间通报，对可能的被埋人员搜寻和遗体打捞工作仍在进行中。事故发生在周日凌晨，垃圾填埋场在暴雨后发生滑动，掩埋了邻近的定居点。几天前，政府因垃圾填埋场变得不稳定而下令疏散该地区并采取安全措施，但显然并非所有居民都遵守了这一命令。流亡的反对派政治家、前政府首脑塞卢·达莱因·迪亚洛在社交媒体Facebook上表示，事故之所以「更加令人不安」，是因为「垃圾填埋场的关闭原定于本周日」进行。他呼吁当局「以完全透明的方式查明导致这场灾难的原因，并从中吸取一切教训」。该国矿产资源丰富，但许多民众贫困。搜索和救援工作仍在继续。总理阿马杜·乌里·巴视察了事故现场，并代表政府向受灾民众表示哀悼。达尔萨拉姆是科纳克里最贫困的地区之一，2017年曾发生过一次造成多人死亡的滑坡事故。尽管拥有丰富的矿产资源，几内亚仍是世界上最贫困的国家之一。这个拥有约1500万人口的西非国家是世界上最重要的铝土矿（铝的主要原料）出口国之一，但许多民众仍无法充分获得医疗服务、教育、电力和清洁饮用水。

articles.title: Frankreich: Raphaël Glucksmann kündigt Kandidatur für Präsidentschaftswahl 2027 an
articles.excerpt: Dieser Ausdruck wurde am 24.08.2026 erstellt und ist ausschließlich für den persönlichen Gebrauch lizenziert.Andere Nutzungen verletzen das Urheberrecht Der französische EU-Abgeordnete Raphaël Glucksmann hat seine Kandidatur für die Präsidentschaftswahl im April 2027 angekündigt. Er könnte als gemeinsamer Kandidat des sozialdemokratischen Lagers antreten. 23.08.2026, 22.49 Uhr Raphaël Glucksmann Foto: Julie Sebadelha / AFP Der französische EU-Abgeordnete Raphaël Glucksmann möchte bei der Präsidentschaftswahl im kommenden Jahr antreten. Der 46-Jährige verkündete seine Kandidatur am Sonntagabend im französischen Fernsehsender TF1.Sein Ziel sei es, »Frankreich wieder aufzurichten«, so Glucksmann. Ob er als gemeinsamer Kandidat des sozialdemokratischen Lagers ins Rennen geht, soll im Oktober entschieden werden. Dann sind Vorwahlen zwischen seiner Partei Place publique und den Sozialisten (PS) geplant. Die Präsidentschaftswahl findet im April 2027 statt. Amtsinhaber Emmanuel Macron kann nach zwei Amtszeiten nicht erneut kandidieren. Aus seinem politischen Lager hat der frühere Premierminister Édouard Philippe bereits seine Ambitionen erklärt.Zwischen Le Pen und MélenchonFür den rechtspopulistischen Rassemblement National (RN) plant Marine Le Pen anzutreten. Ihr werden gute Chancen eingeräumt, die Stichwahl zu erreichen. Mehr zum Thema 4 Min 4 Min 1 Min 4 Min Auch der Linkspopulist Jean-Luc Mélenchon hat seine Kandidatur bereits angekündigt.Mehr über die Lage der französischen Parteipolitik zur Präsidentschaftswahl 2027 und warum sich die politischen Extreme durchsetzen könnten, erfahren Sie hier. dtt/AFP

articles.title: Crans-Montana: Barbetreiber Jacques Moretti wegen häuslicher Gewalt festgenommen
articles.excerpt: Dieser Ausdruck wurde am 24.08.2026 erstellt und ist ausschließlich für den persönlichen Gebrauch lizenziert.Andere Nutzungen verletzen das Urheberrecht Der Besitzer der bei der Brandkatastrophe in Crans-Montana zerstörten Bar sitzt in Untersuchungshaft, weil er seine Ehefrau misshandelt haben soll. Gegen das Paar wird noch immer wegen des Feuers in der Silvesternacht mit 41 Toten ermittelt. 23.08.2026, 22.44 Uhr Barbetreiber Jacques und Jessica Moretti Foto: Fabrice Coffrini / AFP Der Besitzer der bei der Brandkatastrophe im Schweizer Skiort Crans-Montana zerstörten Bar »Le Constellation« sitzt wegen Gewalt gegen seine Ehefrau in Untersuchungshaft.Über die Festnahme des Mannes berichtete zuerst der Fernsehsender Léman Bleu am Sonntag. Demnach soll er seine Frau so schwer misshandelt haben, dass sie ins Krankenhaus gebracht werden musste. Bei dem Brand in der Silvesternacht waren 41 Menschen, darunter überwiegend junge Leute, ums Leben gekommen. 115 weitere wurden verletzt.Ermittlungen zu dem Brandfall dauern anGegen das Barbesitzer-Ehepaar wird wegen fahrlässiger Tötung, fahrlässiger Körperverletzung und fahrlässiger Brandstiftung ermittelt. Mehr zum Thema 2 Min 1 Min 1 Min Die Anwälte des Paares erklärten am Sonntagabend, die neuen Vorwürfe beträfen »ausschließlich das Privatleben« der beiden. Zugleich verwiesen sie auf den Zusammenhang mit der »besonders schweren Prüfung«, der sich das Ehepaar seit dem 1. Januar stellen müsse. dtt/AFP

articles.title: Hockey-WM: Deutsche Männer drehen Rückstand in 62 Sekunden und stehen im Halbfinale
articles.excerpt: Deutschlands Hockey-Männer stehen im Halbfinale der Weltmeisterschaft. Der Titelverteidiger setzte sich im letzten Zwischenrundenspiel im belgischen Wavre 4:2 (3:2) gegen Australien durch und ist damit nicht mehr von einem der ersten beiden Plätze in der Gruppe F zu verdrängen. »Das ist der helle Wahnsinn. Das war unsere mit Abstand beste Leistung«, sagte Bundestrainer André Henning bei »MagentaSport«. Der Europameister benötigte nach der 1:2-Niederlage gegen Spanien einen Sieg, um aus eigener Kraft in die Runde der letzten Vier einzuziehen.Zunächst hatten Hannes Müller (11. Minute) und Michel Struthoff (12.) mit ihren ersten Turniertoren den frühen Rückstand durch Blake Govers (3.) innerhalb von nur 62 Sekunden gedreht, ehe Justus Warweg (19.) im zweiten Viertel auf 3:1 erhöhte. Mehr zum Thema 1 Min Der Halbfinalgegner steht noch ausAustralien verkürzte kurz vor der Pause durch Joel Rintala (30.) auf 2:3. Der Weltmeister nahm den Videobeweis, doch die korrekte Ausführung wurde bestätigt und Deutschland verlor damit sein Anrufrecht. Im dritten Viertel verwandelte Hugo von Montgelas (40.) die dritte Strafecke zum 4:2, auch für ihn war es das erste WM-Tor. Im Schlussviertel erhöhten die »Kookaburras« noch einmal den Druck, aber die deutsche Defensive um Kapitän Tom Grambusch ließ nichts mehr zu. Der Halbfinalgegner für den Freitagabend entscheidet sich erst am Montag zwischen Olympiasieger und Co-Gastgeber Niederlande sowie Argentinien, England und Indien. Linnea Weidemann (hier im Gruppenspiel gegen Argentinien) Foto: Nordphoto / Memmler / IMAGO Deutsche Spielerinnen bereits ausgeschiedenFür die deutschen Hockey-Frauen ist der Traum vom Halbfinale bei der WM in Belgien und den Niederlanden hingegen geplatzt.

articles.title: Iran: Parlamentspräsident droht USA mit Bumerang-Effekt im Wirtschaftskrieg
articles.excerpt: Säbelrasseln in den sozialen Medien: Der iranische Parlamentspräsident Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf hat die USA angesichts der von Washington geplanten verschärften Sanktionen gegen die Islamische Republik vor einem Bumerang-Effekt gewarnt.Auf der Plattform X teilte er einen Comic, der insinuierte, dass der von Washington angekündigte Wirtschaftskrieg die USA selbst treffen werde. »Eine eingefrorene Außenpolitik bringt eine eingefrorene Wirtschaft hervor«, schrieb Ghalibaf – und spielte dabei auch auf die gestiegenen Renditen amerikanischer Staatsanleihen an. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte am Mittwoch angekündigt, den wirtschaftlichen Druck auf Iran drastisch erhöhen zu wollen. Er sprach von einem »wirtschaftlichen D-Day« für Iran. Er drohte auch Unterstützern Teherans mit drakonischen Maßnahmen. Details zu seinen Plänen lieferte Trump zunächst nicht. Empfohlener externer Inhalt An dieser Stelle finden Sie einen externen Inhalt von X.com, der den Artikel ergänzt und von der Redaktion empfohlen wird. Sie können Ihre Zustimmung jederzeit wieder zurücknehmen. Externen Inhalt anzeigen Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung. US-Finanzminister Scott Bessent will am Montag auf einer Pressekonferenz über das Vorhaben informieren und sprach von den »härtesten Sanktionen der Geschichte«, die man verhängen wolle. Wirtschaft unter DruckIranische Staatsmedien hatten sich nach Trumps Ansage gelassen gegeben. Die USA versuchten seit Jahren, jegliche finanzielle und wirtschaftlichen Beziehungen zum Iran zu unterbinden, schrieb etwa die Nachrichtenagentur Tasnim. Iran habe jedoch »gelernt, diese Beschränkungen zu umgehen, und ist darin mittlerweile sehr versiert«. Trotz des ausgeklügelten Systems zur Umgehung der Sanktionen ist die wirtschaftliche Entwicklung in Iran jedoch seit Jahren massiv unter Druck.

articles.title: Senegal und Mauretanien stoppen Hunderte Bootsmigranten
articles.excerpt: Bereits am Donnerstag hatte die Marine eigenen Angaben zufolge 246 Geflüchtete vor der senegalesischen Küste aufgegriffen.Lebensgefährlicher Weg zu den KanarenIn Mauretanien rettete die Küstenwache am Mittwoch 315 Menschen aus einem Holzboot. Das Schiff war demnach in Gambia gestartet. Unter den Geretteten seien auch Säuglinge gewesen.Immer wieder versuchen Menschen, von der westafrikanischen Küste aus über den Atlantik auf die zu Spanien gehörenden Kanarischen Inseln zu gelangen. Die Route ist lebensgefährlich. Nach einem Rekord bei den Ankünften auf den Kanaren im Jahr 2024 ist die Zahl der irregulären Überfahrten zuletzt deutlich zurückgegangen. Bis Mitte Juli kamen in diesem Jahr nach Angaben der Vereinten Nationen rund 4400 Menschen auf diesem Weg auf den Inseln an – etwa 60 Prozent weniger als im Vorjahreszeitraum.

articles.title: DFB-Pokal: FC St. Pauli scheitert in der ersten Runde an Rot-Weiss Essen
articles.excerpt: Damit wartet das Team von Trainer Marcel Rapp weiter auf den ersten Pflichtspielsieg der Saison. In der 2. Liga gab es lediglich Unentschieden gegen die SpVgg Greuther Fürth (1:1) und bei Holstein Kiel (2:2).Die Essener, Pokalsieger von 1953, zogen damit in die zweite Runde ein. Marek Janssen brachte den Beinahe-Aufsteiger, der in der Zweitliga-Relegation an Fürth gescheitert war, im Stadion an der Hafenstraße in Führung (36.). Semir Telalovic erhöhte kurz nach der Pause (53.). Vor einem Jahr war RWE trotz starker Leistung gegen Borussia Dortmund (0:1) ausgeschieden. St. Pauli hatte in der ersten Hälfte die besseren Torchancen, doch Martijn Kaars scheiterte gleich zweimal in aussichtsreicher Position (19./31.). Auf der Gegenseite verwertete Janssen eine Flanke von Marvin Obuz per Kopf zum 1:0. Nach dem zweiten Gegentreffer waren die Gäste sichtlich geschockt, offensiv fiel den Hamburgern wenig ein, Essen hatte das Spiel im Griff. Freiburg und Paderborn mit SiegenBesser machte es der SC Freiburg. Der Bundesligist hat sich durch ein 5:1 (1:0) bei Fortuna Düsseldorf für die zweite Runde qualifiziert. In der Neuauflage des Zweitrundenspiels aus dem Vorjahr erzielten Lucas Höler (18.), Joker Igor Matanović (71., 90.+4), Lukas Kübler (74.) und Jordy Makengo (80.) die Treffer für die überlegenen Gäste, die in der vergangenen Saison bis ins Halbfinale vorgestoßen waren. Die Fortuna, für die Fabian Schleusener traf (76.), verlor nach dem Abstieg in die 3. Liga auch ihr drittes Spiel in der laufenden Spielzeit. Auch Bundesliga-Aufsteiger SC Paderborn ist mit einem Erfolgserlebnis in die Saison gestartet. Beim Pflichtspielauftakt im DFB-Pokal gewannen die Ostwestfalen 4:2 (2:1) beim Regionalligisten 1. articles.title: Italien könnte neues EU-Asylsystem »sprengen«, warnt CDU-Innenexperte Throm
articles.excerpt: Der Streit über die Rücknahme von Asylbewerbern nach den Dublin-Regeln schwelt weiter. Italien weigert sich, Migranten aus Deutschland aufzunehmen. Nun legt Unionspolitiker Alexander Throm nach. 23.08.2026, 20.55 Uhr CDU-Innenpolitiker Throm Foto: Elisa Schu / dpa Im Streit über die Rücknahme von Migranten hat der innenpolitische Sprecher der Unionsfraktion, Alexander Throm, Italien vorgeworfen, das neue europäische Asylsystem zu torpedieren. »Wenn Italien diese Haltung beibehält, sprengt es das neue Gemeinsame Europäische Asylsystem (Geas), das erst seit wenigen Wochen in Kraft ist«, sagte der CDU-Politiker der Deutschen Presse-Agentur. Ohne die Rücknahme derjenigen Asylbewerber, für deren Asylverfahren Italien zuständig sei, müssten die Kontrollen an den deutschen Grenzen nicht nur beibehalten, sondern intensiviert werden. Dies würde eine Kettenreaktion in anderen europäischen Ländern nach sich ziehen, vermutete Throm.Seit Mitte Juni gelten in der EU die neuen Geas-Regeln für den Umgang mit Asylsuchenden. Das System sieht im Kern zwei Neuerungen vor: Einerseits Grenzverfahren und schnelle Abschiebungen bei Asylbewerbern aus vergleichsweise sicheren Staaten.Andererseits eine Art neuen Deal zwischen Staaten an der Außengrenze und jenen in der Mitte des Kontinents. Besonders belastete Länder an den Außengrenzen sollen von weniger belasteten unterstützt werden – zum Beispiel durch Geldzahlungen. Im Gegenzug sollen, so die Idee, die Dublin-Regeln wieder eingehalten werden, wonach jener EU-Staat für das Asylverfahren zuständig ist, den ein irregulärer Migrant zuerst betritt. Das betrifft vor allem Staaten wie Italien, Spanien und Griechenland – die deshalb bisher viele Migranten einfach weiterreisen ließen.Insbesondere Italien hatte sich seit 2023 geweigert, weitergereiste Asylsuchende zurückzunehmen.

articles.title: Sonnenfinsternis verpasst? Jetzt kommt die Mondfinsternis
articles.excerpt: Nach Sonnenfinsternis und Sternschnuppennächten ist die Zeit der besonderen Himmelsereignisse im August noch nicht vorbei: In wenigen Tagen wird eine teilweise, eine partielle Mondfinsternis erwartet. Bei einer Mondfinsternis sind Sonne, Mond und Erde annähernd auf gleicher Linie. Der Mond befindet sich dann im Kernschatten der Erde und wird dadurch verfinstert. Am Morgen des 28. August tritt der Mond um 4.34 Uhr in den Kernschatten der Erde ein. Wegen der nur partiellen Mondfinsternis falle dieser Schatten nur auf einen Teil der Mondoberfläche, sagte Carolin Liefke, stellvertretende Leiterin des Hauses der Astronomie in Heidelberg. Ein Teil des Mondes bleibe hell.»Man sollte früh aufstehen und sich genau wie auch bei der Sonnenfinsternis einen erhöhten Platz suchen«, sagte Liefke. Je weiter man im Westen wohne, desto besser sei das Spektakel zu sehen. Eine Brille wie bei der Sonnenfinsternis ist zum Anschauen nicht nötig. Um halb fünf geht es los»Der Beginn der partiellen Phase kurz nach halb fünf lässt sich gut sehen: Der Mond steht hoch am Himmel, es ist noch dunkle Nacht«, sagte der Vorsitzende der Vereinigung der Sternfreunde mit Sitz im südhessischen Bensheim, Uwe Pilz, der Nachrichtenagentur dpa.Später werde die Beobachtung schwerer fallen. Der Vollmond wird mit bis zu etwa 94 Prozent seines Durchmessers in den Kernschatten der Erde eintreten. »Das Maximum tritt kurz nach sechs Uhr ein«, sagt Pilz. Wegen des nahen Monduntergangs und des Sonnenaufgangs sei dies praktisch nicht zu sehen. »Trotz der Einschränkungen ist diese Mondfinsternis ein lohnendes Schauspiel«, sagte Pilz.

articles.title: Griechenland: Krawalle in Migrantenunterkunft Sintiki
articles.excerpt: Bei schweren Ausschreitungen in einer geschlossenen Unterkunft für Migranten sind im Norden Griechenlands fünf Menschen verletzt und 17 festgenommen worden. In der Einrichtung in der Gemeinde Sintiki nahe der Grenze zu Bulgarien kam es nach Angaben der Sicherheitsbehörden zu gewaltsamen Auseinandersetzungen zwischen Migranten und der Polizei. Dies berichtete der öffentlich-rechtliche Rundfunk ERTNews. Die Unruhen begannen nach Angaben griechischer Medien am Samstagabend. Eine Gruppe von Migranten soll zunächst einen Teil der inneren Umzäunung niedergerissen und anschließend Steine und andere Gegenstände auf die eingesetzten Polizisten geworfen haben. Bei den Ausschreitungen wurden demnach Gebäude, Gemeinschaftsbereiche, Überwachungskameras und weitere Einrichtungen beschädigt.Verletzte ins Krankenhaus gebrachtDen Angaben zufolge gelang es einigen Migranten, einen Teil des äußeren Drahtzauns zu durchtrennen und das Gelände zu verlassen. Drei von ihnen wurden noch vor Ort von der Polizei festgehalten. Weitere 14 wurden wenig später in der Umgebung festgenommen.

articles.title: Alibaba: Chinesischer Onlineriese plant milliardenschwere Kapitalerhöhung für KI
articles.excerpt: Im Wettlauf um das Geschäft mit künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) möchte sich der chinesische Onlineriese Alibaba bei Investoren frisches Geld holen. Wie der Konzern mitteilte, sollen durch den Verkauf neuer Aktien an der Börse ‌in Hongkong insgesamt 80 Milliarden Hongkong-Dollar (rund 8,73 Milliarden Euro) eingenommen werden. Dem Unternehmen zufolge handelt es sich um die größte Kapitalerhöhung eines in Hongkong gelisteten Unternehmens. Zudem ist es die weltweit drittgrößte Transaktion dieser Art in diesem Jahr, nach ähnlichen Schritten der US-Technologiekonzerne Alphabet und Intel.Laut Informationen der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters plant Alibaba den Verkauf von 710 Millionen Stammaktien zu einem Preis von je 112,70 Hongkong-Dollar. ​Dies entspricht einem Abschlag von 3,6 Prozent gegenüber dem jüngsten Schlusskurs. US-Investoren sind von der Transaktion ausgeschlossen, da die Platzierung nach ​Angaben von Alibaba nicht nach ‌US-Wertpapiergesetzen registriert wurde. Noch mehr RechenleistungDie Einnahmen aus dem Aktienverkauf will Alibaba nach eigenen Angaben vollständig in den KI-Bereich stecken. Geplant seien Investitionen in die gesamte Bandbreite der KI-Technologie. Dazu gehörten auch der Ausbau und die Verbesserung der dafür notwendigen Infrastruktur wie etwa Rechenzentren. Konkret solle das Geld in sogenannte Full-Stack-KI-Kapazitäten fließen, was neben der ‌Infrastruktur auch Chips sowie die Entwicklung und den Einsatz von KI-Modellen umfasst. In der vergangenen Woche hatte Alibaba seine Zahlen für das erste Geschäftsquartal vorgelegt. Der Nettogewinn brach im Vergleich zum Vorjahr um 75 Prozent ein, was der Konzern ‌mit den gestiegenen Investitionen in KI begründete.Alibaba hat fast ​die Hälfte des Geldes ausgegeben, das in einem dreijährigen Investitionsplan vorgesehen war, der im vorigen Jahr anlief. Die erwartete Zeitspanne, innerhalb derer sich KI-Investitionen ‌rechneten, habe sich jedoch dank der boomenden Nachfrage von 3 auf 2,5 Jahre verkürzt.

articles.title: Welche Karten müssen Sie umdrehen? - Rätsel der Woche
articles.excerpt: Es geht beim neuen Rätsel um keinen Kartentrick, sondern um Logik. Vier Spielkarten liegen vor uns. Wir wissen, dass auf der Vorderseite jeder Karte eine Zahl steht. Und dass die Rückseiten entweder blau oder rot sind – siehe Abbildung oben.Außerdem soll folgende Regel gelten: Wenn die Zahl auf der Vorderseite einer Karte gerade ist, soll ihre Rückseite blau sein. Welche der vier Karten müssen Sie umdrehen, um zu überprüfen, ob diese Regel tatsächlich bei allen Karten eingehalten wird? Gesucht werden die kleinstmögliche Anzahl und natürlich die konkreten umzudrehenden Karten. Wir müssen zwei Karten umdrehen: die Karte mit der 8 und die rote Karte.Dass wir die 8 umdrehen müssen, ist klar. Sollte die Rückseite rot sein, wäre die Regel verletzt. Also müssen wir die Rückseite der 8 überprüfen. Die 3 können wir ignorieren. Die Farbe der Rückseite ist irrelevant, weil es für Karten mit ungerader Zahl keine Regel gibt. Die Rückseite kann daher blau oder rot sein, ohne der vorgegebenen Regel zu widersprechen. Schwieriger ist die Entscheidung bei der roten und der blauen Karte. Hier ist man versucht, die blaue Karte umzudrehen. Das ist aber unnötig. Denn eine blaue Rückseite sagt über die Vorderseite gar nichts aus – die Zahl auf der Vorderseite kann gerade oder ungerade sein, beides ist regelkonform. Von den beiden Karten, deren Farbseite sichtbar ist, müssen wir nur die rote Karte umdrehen. Denn es könnte ja sein, dass auf der anderen Seite der roten Karte eine gerade Zahl steht, was ein Verstoß gegen die Regel wäre. Daher muss diese Karte zwingend umgedreht werden. Insgesamt müssen wir somit genau zwei Karten umdrehen: die 8 und die rote Karte. Diese Logikaufgabe geht auf den englischen Psychologen Peter Wason zurück und wird als »Wason Selection Task« bezeichnet. Bei seinen Tests fanden gerade mal zehn Prozent der Probanden die richtige Lösung.Eine interessante Erkenntnis brachten Versuche mit leicht verändertem Setting.

articles.title: Formel 1 – Großer Preis der Niederlande: Heftiger Unfall von Max Verstappen
articles.excerpt: Max Verstappen ist nach einem heftigen Unfall auf der ersten Runde beim Großen Preis der Niederlande ausgeschieden. Der viermalige Formel-1-Weltmeister verlor in der Steilkurve vor der Start- und Zielgeraden die Kontrolle über seinen Red Bull.Er krachte mit dem Wagen mit Wucht in die Streckenmauer und rutschte auf dem noch feuchten Kurs mit dem demolierten Auto zurück auf die Strecke. Der 28 Jahre alte Verstappen stieg aus eigener Kraft wieder aus und schien zunächst unverletzt, weitere Informationen gibt es noch nicht. Empfohlener externer Inhalt An dieser Stelle finden Sie einen externen Inhalt von X.com, der den Artikel ergänzt und von der Redaktion empfohlen wird. Sie können Ihre Zustimmung jederzeit wieder zurücknehmen. Externen Inhalt anzeigen Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung. »Sorry«, funkte er an die Box. Das Rennen war vorübergehend unterbrochen.Der Red Bull wurde stark beschädigtVorn lag zu diesem Zeitpunkt Weltmeister Lando Norris (McLaren) vor Kimi Antonelli und George Russell (beide Mercedes). Der zerstörte Red Bull Foto: John Thys / AFP Die Formel 1 ist an diesem Wochenende zum vorerst letzten Mal in Zandvoort zu Gast. Der Grand Prix am Sonntag markiert den Abschied der Niederlande aus dem Rennkalender. Verstappen hatte nach der Rückkehr in den Rennkalender 2021, 2022 und 2023 dort gewonnen, in den vergangenen beiden Jahren war der Red-Bull-Star auf Platz zwei gefahren. Er hatte unter der Woche seinen Vertrag bei Red Bull verlängert.

articles.title: DFB-Pokal: 1. FC Heidenheim blamiert sich gegen Regionalligist Jeddeloh II
articles.excerpt: Fußball-Regionalligist SSV Jeddeloh II hat im DFB-Pokal für eine Sensation gesorgt. Der Außenseiter besiegte den Bundesligaabsteiger 1. FC Heidenheim im Oldenburger Marschweg-Stadion 5:2 (3:1). Die Heidenheimer traten ohne ihren gesperrten Langzeittrainer Frank Schmidt an und erlebten eine Blamage. Schmidt verfolgte das Spiel von der Tribüne aus. Drei Gegentore binnen einer ViertelstundeDabei waren die Favoriten dank des Treffers von Yannik Wagner noch in Führung gegangen (12. Minute) – doch schnell nahm das Pokaldebakel der Heidenheimer seinen Lauf. Nur zwei Minuten später glich Kamer Krasniqi (14.) aus. Ein Eigentor von Jan Schöppner (27.) und ein Traumtor von Haris Hyseni (29.) führten bereits zu einem klaren Pausenrückstand. Mehr zum Thema 2 Min 3 Min 3 Min Zu Beginn der zweiten Hälfte verschoss der eingewechselte Budu Siwsiwadse einen selbst herausgeholten Foulelfmeter für Heidenheim. Der Zweitligist bemühte sich um den Anschluss – doch mit einem Konter holte auch Jeddeloh II einen Strafstoß heraus: Hyseni erhöhte mit seinem zweiten Treffer (70.) auf 4:1. Tim Janßen ließ die Heidenheimer noch schlechter aussehen (72.). Mikkel Kaufmann (89.) gelang nur noch Ergebniskosmetik. Ungewohnte Situation für beide TrainerFCH-Coach Schmidt sah aus ungewohnter Position auf der Tribüne, wie sich die eklatante Defensivschwäche seines Teams fortsetzte. In nur drei Pflichtspielen in dieser Saison kassierte der Ostalb-Club nun zwölf Gegentore. Der 52-jährige Schmidt war wegen einer Gelb-Roten-Karte aus der vergangenen DFB-Pokal-Saison gesperrt und wurde von Co-Trainer Bernhard Raab vertreten. Frank Schmidt sah das Debakel von der Tribüne aus Foto: Carmen Jaspersen / dpa Auch für Jeddelohs Trainer Kristian Arambasic war der Nachmittag ungewohnt. Zum fünften Mal ist Arambasic im DFB-Pokal dabei – und das mit dem vierten Verein. Erstmals schaffte der 49-Jährige den Einzug in die zweite Runde.

articles.title: 大分で39度予想 熊本も危険な暑さに 熱中症対策の徹底を
articles.excerpt: 24日も西日本と東日本の各地で気温が上がり、大分県では最高気温が39度と危険な暑さとなる見込みです。熊本県の被災地でも危険な暑さになる見込みで、熱中症対策を徹底してください。
articles.summary: 24日，日本西部和东部多地气温上升，大分县预计最高气温达39度，熊本县灾区也面临危险高温，当局呼吁民众彻底做好防中暑措施。
